title: Deprecated options: a warning when used, a mark in the help, the typings
request: Add `Option#deprecated(message?)` so a CLI can retire an option gently. It returns the option (for chaining). A deprecated option still works exactly as before, but when it is given on the command line commander writes ONE warning per parse to the error output (the command's `writeErr` from `configureOutput`): `warning: option '<flags>' is deprecated: <message>` followed by a newline, or `warning: option '<flags>' is deprecated` when there is no message, where <flags> is the option's flags as declared (e.g. `--old-name <value>`). It is not an error and does not stop the action. No warning when the value only comes from a default or an environment variable. This must work for options of subcommands too. In the help, a deprecated option's line says `deprecated` (next to the default/env information). Add it to the TypeScript typings.

title: A client can spoof req.ip behind one proxy (the cause is two modules away)
request: Security report from a customer: their app runs behind exactly one load balancer and sets `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` as the docs say. Find out why and fix it.

title: "Make not-found better for our API clients"
request: Our API clients get an HTML page back when they call a URL that doesn't exist, which their code can't read. Can you make not-found handling in express better for them?

ask.question: What should an API client get for a URL that does not exist: a JSON body (with which fields?), or only a status code? And should HTML clients keep today's page?
options: JSON with the method and path, HTML stays

answers.say: Here is exactly what I mean. When no route matches and the client prefers JSON (its Accept header picks json over html, as `req.accepts(['html', 'json'])` says), respond 404 with `Content-Type: application/json` and exactly the body `{"error":"Not Found","method":"GET","path":"/the/path"}`: the request's method, and the full path the client asked for (inside a mounted app too) without the query string. Clients that prefer HTML or accept anything keep today's HTML page, routes that exist are untouched, and errors (`next(err)`) still go to the normal error handling. Do it in express itself, for every app.

rubric: The bot asked about the detail that was actually missing (what the not-found response should look like for API clients), not about things it could see in the code
The question is short and specific, with at most a few options
It did not start changing code before it had the answer, and did not invent requirements the person never gave
